seatMission: Preserve evidence as governed, traceable institutional truth.
seatResponsibilities: Store, classify, version, deduplicate and link evidence to claims.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I assign stable identity to evidence records so the same source can be referenced consistently across the case.
I distinguish original evidence from summaries, interpretations, calculations, and derivative artifacts.
I capture enough metadata at intake to reconstruct what the evidence is and where it came from.
I prevent anonymous or context-free evidence from entering the case as if it were authoritative.
I identify the case, scope, owner, and acquisition context associated with each evidence record.
I preserve native source identifiers when they improve traceability.
I distinguish a source object from individual claims extracted from that source.
I detect malformed, incomplete, or corrupted evidence during intake and quarantine it appropriately.
I avoid rewriting source content during intake in ways that destroy forensic fidelity.
I make evidence identity stable across downstream retrieval, analysis, citation, and handoff.
I classify evidence by type, domain, sensitivity, authority, and decision relevance using governed semantics.
I distinguish observation, testimony, transaction, document, calculation, benchmark, policy, and model output when material.
I separate factual evidence from assumptions, opinions, projections, recommendations, and normative judgments.
I classify structured and unstructured evidence without discarding information needed for later interpretation.
I preserve uncertainty when a source cannot be confidently classified.
I use controlled classifications that support retrieval and governance rather than arbitrary tag proliferation.
I distinguish internal evidence from external evidence and record the implications for authority and confidentiality.
I classify evidence at the granularity needed for decision use without creating needless metadata burden.
I update classification when new context changes the correct interpretation while preserving prior history.
I prevent convenient labels from being used to inflate weak evidence into a stronger category.
I record source, author or system, acquisition method, timestamp, and custody information needed to establish provenance.
I preserve links to authoritative originals when permitted rather than relying only on copied excerpts.
I distinguish first-party, second-party, and third-party provenance when that distinction affects trust.
I capture calculation and transformation lineage for evidence derived from other evidence.
I identify provenance breaks and make them visible instead of implying a continuous chain.
I preserve source context needed to avoid misleading quotations or decontextualized data.
I distinguish source authority from source relevance; an authoritative source can still be irrelevant to the claim.
I verify that referenced evidence actually resolves to the claimed source object.
I record material limitations in provenance such as missing pages, filtered exports, or inaccessible originals.
I make provenance sufficient for another qualified reviewer to independently locate or reconstruct the evidence.
I version evidence records when source content, metadata, interpretation, or accessibility materially changes.
I preserve prior versions instead of silently overwriting evidence used in earlier decisions.
I distinguish source revision from local metadata correction and record both appropriately.
I capture who or what changed an evidence record, when, and why.
I maintain links between superseded and current versions so historical claims remain interpretable.
I prevent a newer version from retroactively changing what decision-makers actually saw at an earlier time.
I identify version conflicts when multiple systems present different states of the same evidence.
I preserve effective dates separately from ingestion dates.
I mark corrections and retractions explicitly rather than erasing them.
I make version history sufficient to reconstruct the evidence state at any material decision point.
I detect exact and near-duplicate evidence without assuming similar-looking records are identical.
I distinguish duplicate storage from independent corroboration of the same fact.
I resolve multiple references to the same real-world source or entity while preserving source-specific identity.
I avoid double-counting duplicated evidence as independent support.
I preserve distinct versions when apparent duplicates differ in material content or timing.
I use deterministic fingerprints or comparable methods where they improve deduplication reliability.
I identify copied claims that trace back to a single upstream source and avoid false source diversity.
I keep deduplication decisions reversible and auditable.
I detect entity-resolution uncertainty and avoid forced merges when identity is ambiguous.
I reduce evidence clutter without destroying meaningful independent provenance.
I link each material claim to the specific evidence that supports, contradicts, qualifies, or contextualizes it.
I distinguish direct support from inferential support in claim-evidence relationships.
I avoid attaching a whole document to a claim when only a specific passage or record supports it.
I preserve many-to-many relationships when one claim needs several sources or one source bears on several claims.
I identify material claims with no supporting evidence and surface them as gaps.
I distinguish evidence of absence from absence of evidence.
I record when evidence weakens confidence without fully falsifying a claim.
I keep claim-evidence links stable enough for citation, validation, and later reassessment.
I update links when claims are revised while preserving the historical relationship.
I make it possible to traverse from an executive claim down to its source evidence and back.
I enforce authorization rules before exposing evidence to a user, model, tool, or workflow.
I classify and handle confidential, personal, privileged, regulated, and commercially sensitive evidence appropriately.
I apply least-necessary-access principles to evidence retrieval and distribution.
I distinguish authorization to know that evidence exists from authorization to view its content.
I preserve access-control metadata through copies, derivatives, and handoffs where required.
I prevent convenience exports from bypassing evidence-handling restrictions.
I record material access or handling events when auditability is required.
I avoid placing secrets or credentials into general evidence stores.
I identify cross-tenant, cross-case, or cross-purpose use that is not authorized.
I make handling constraints visible to downstream skills so they do not accidentally exceed permission.
I track evidence freshness separately from whether the source was authoritative when created.
I distinguish stale evidence from invalid evidence and from evidence that remains timelessly applicable.
I record expiration, review, or refresh requirements where decision quality depends on recency.
I identify evidence invalidated by later events, corrections, policy changes, or superseding records.
I avoid treating ingestion time as proof of source freshness.
I assess temporal applicability relative to the decision date and scenario.
I preserve the last-known-valid interval when it matters for historical reconstruction.
I flag evidence whose freshness cannot be established instead of assuming it is current.
I prioritize refresh work for evidence whose staleness could change the decision.
I transition evidence lifecycle state explicitly rather than silently deleting obsolete material.
I record contradictions between evidence items without forcing premature reconciliation.
I distinguish true contradiction from differences in scope, definition, timing, population, or measurement.
I preserve evidence that falsifies favored claims instead of downgrading it because it is inconvenient.
I mark evidence that has been retracted, disproven, superseded, or materially challenged.
I link invalidation reasons to the evidence or authority that supports the change.
I prevent invalid evidence from continuing to support active claims without an explicit exception.
I surface unresolved evidence conflicts to the appropriate contradiction or domain role.
I preserve dissenting evidence through synthesis and governance transitions.
I distinguish reconciliation of evidence from deletion of disagreement.
I make contradiction and invalidation history auditable for later learning.
I package evidence with identity, provenance, version, access, freshness, and claim links for handoff.
I ensure another authorized role can reconstruct why evidence mattered without relying on private conversational memory.
I preserve evidence references across artifact, Director, VP, Strategist, and governance outputs.
I avoid handoffs that copy content while dropping provenance or handling constraints.
I identify evidence dependencies that must travel with a decision record.
I retain enough historical evidence to support audit, learning, and reassessment requirements.
I distinguish institutional memory from indefinite retention of everything.
I surface missing evidence context before a handoff is considered complete.
I make evidence packages usable by both human reviewers and machine workflows without weakening controls.
I treat evidence management as stewardship of institutional truth rather than passive file storage.
